_comment: st_4312c9c0. Declares the LANE every model call site may run at, and why. Lanes are provider-agnostic: 'fast' | 'balanced' | 'best' resolve to a concrete model through config/models.json, so switching provider or model generation is a config change, never an edit to this file or to any call site. Enforced by scripts/check-tier-policy-match.js, which DISCOVERS call sites by scanning the tree — a new one that is not declared here fails the commit rather than going unnoticed.
_provider_note: The active provider for application calls. Every lane below resolves through config/models.json for THIS provider. Change this one field to move the whole application to google, openai, or xai — the per-provider lane table already exists and lib/llm/ carries an adapter for each. Nothing in this file names a model. 2026-08-14: owner set xAI/Grok as the default for chat and metered API spend. Anthropic remains selectable in the chat UI.

_lanes.fast: Cheapest tier. Mechanical work: extraction, classification, routing, dedup, bulk sweeps.
_lanes.balanced: Mid tier. Substrate synthesis, and mechanical work whose input is hard enough that the cheap lane fails on it.
_lanes.best: Top tier. Reserved. Nothing runs here by default — a site on 'best' should carry an explicit reason and the owner's approval.

_categories.substrate: Output is persisted and read back into a later prompt. Mechanical test: does anything on the prompt-assembly path read this file or table. Held at a capable lane because an error compounds into every downstream answer and cannot be traced back.
_categories.mechanical: Everything else. Read once, then discarded or stored where no prompt reads it. Cheapest lane that does the job.
_categories.infrastructure: Names a model constant without choosing a tier for itself — gateways, registries, pickers, reverse-maps. No lane to enforce.

_persona_note: Personas run on the Claude Code subscription, not the metered key — billed as allowance, not dollars. The rule is not 'cheapest' but 'cheapest that does not cause a rerun': a failed stage costs a full second pass, which is more allowance than the lane saved. Bulk retrieval goes fast; anything that designs, builds, or checks stays balanced.

lib/conversations.js.why: Live-thread compact. One-shot summarization of old messages; not a standing prompt layer.

lib/topic-session.js.why: Writes the topic LOG resume that the next session injects on turns 1-3.

lib/topic-context.js.why: The topic summary is a standing prompt layer, injected on every chat turn for that topic.

lib/entity-card.js.why: Entity cards for the highest-signal people are a standing prompt layer. Lower-signal entities already resolve to the fast lane through contextTierFromN2.

lib/generate-user-md.js.why: Writes the owner's USER.md — the identity card, a standing prompt layer.

lib/voice-ingest.js.why: Writes the owner-voice calibration corpus that governs every future piece of prose written in his name.

lib/profile-research.js.why: Writes persistent entity profile documents, architecturally parallel to entity-card.js.

scripts/synthesize-brief.js.why: Writes the world brief, read into every prompt via buildBriefBlock in lib/chat/system-prompt.js.

scripts/memory-synthesize.js.why: Writes agents/agents.md, which shapes every response.

scripts/ingest/07-context.js.why: Generates the entity context cards; routes per-entity so only the highest-signal people reach the balanced lane.

lib/health-intel.js.why: Writes health_intel DB rows the health UI renders; nothing on the prompt-assembly path reads them back, so it is mechanical by the read-back test. HELD at the top lane deliberately, against the sealed plan's drop to cheapest: a full regeneration is ~$1.00, auto-regeneration is off by default so it fires only on the owner's explicit request, and lifetime spend is ~$12. Trading medical-synthesis quality for single-digit dollars is the wrong side of the trade. Lowering it needs no approval.

lib/health-coach.js.why: Fitness photo and chat interpretation. Daily plans are deterministic; the model only reads a photo or a constraint and writes a JSON guess the owner can edit.

lib/doc-extract.js.why: Document extraction to DB. Escalates from the fast lane on hard documents; nothing downstream reads the output into a prompt.

lib/health-marker-copy.js.why: Per-marker display copy written to DB rows for the health UI. Read once by the renderer, never by a prompt.

scripts/states/delaware-model.js.why: Valuation modelling read once by its caller. Escalates for the DCF step only.

lib/identity-distill.js.why: A pure library — writes nothing, and neither of its two callers writes the identity-card path. Verified rather than assumed.

lib/context-router.js.why: Routing decision, read once. The highest-frequency call site in the system — it fires on every prompt — so the lane matters more here by volume than anywhere else.

lib/attribute-residual.js.why: Residual attribution the deterministic matcher could not settle.

lib/entity-enrich.js.why: Bulk iteration across the corpus — the largest expected dollar line, and the target for the batch discount.

lib/followup-sweep.js.why: Post-call extraction and synthesis into Asana rows.

lib/granola-call-asana.js.why: Transcript summary into an Asana task body.

lib/workbench-promote-entities.js.why: Compaction fallback when a promoted body exceeds its cap.

lib/receipt-extract.js.why: Structured field extraction from receipt images.

lib/doc-classify.js.why: Document type classification — the bulk-classification shape the fast lane exists for.

lib/public-chat/core.js.why: Public marketing chat. Internet-facing and rate-limited; must stay cheapest because the caller is a stranger.

lib/health-pdf-ocr.js.why: OCR fallback for lab PDFs whose text layer is missing. Output lands in health rows, not in a prompt.

lib/chat-tools/white/assistant-mention.j.why: Resolves an @-mention inside a chat turn. Read once, in-turn.

lib/quarantine/tier-1/index.js.why: Quarantined tier-1 classification. Bulk shape, and quarantined code must never be the thing that raises spend.

scripts/enrich-places.js.why: Place enrichment. Bulk, and place cards are not a standing prompt layer.

scripts/extract-all-pdfs.js.why: Bulk PDF text extraction to DB.

scripts/import-pdf-labs.js.why: Lab PDF import — structured extraction to health rows.

scripts/import-pdf-labs-batch.js.why: Batch form of the lab import. Bulk by construction.

scripts/ingest/adjudicate-email-classifi.why: Adjudicates only the residual the deterministic tier could not settle — the canonical Tier-0-then-Tier-1 shape.

routes/chat.js.why: Interactive chat. The owner picks the model in the UI; this ceiling bounds what the route will honour by default.

lib/writing.js.why: Live Miyagi replies and owner nested drafts. One-shot generate; not a standing prompt layer.

infrastructure.lib/compute-tier.js: Canonical model-id and pricing table. Names every constant by definition.
infrastructure.lib/llm-gateway.js: The single choke point. Its reverse-map must name every constant to resolve a caller's model back to a tier.
infrastructure.lib/llm-batch.js: Batch lane. Same reverse-map requirement as the gateway.
infrastructure.lib/llm/anthropic.js: Provider adapter. Translates lane and cache hints for the SDK.
infrastructure.lib/config.js: Holds the per-provider lane table the resolver reads.
infrastructure.lib/chat-ttft-estimator.js: Latency estimation keyed by model; makes no call.
infrastructure.routes/accounts.js: Account/model surface for the UI; makes no call of its own.
infrastructure.scripts/check-tier-policy-match.js: This gate. Necessarily names the constants it matches.
infrastructure.scripts/update-models.js: Refreshes the per-provider catalog. Rewrites which model a lane resolves to, never which lane a caller asks for.
